label: GO step choosing a1, late in the episode
explanation: Mostly a GO-phase feature (92% of mass at GO, 8% at D1, never at D2), active almost only when the policy picks a1 (model_act==1 holds 90% of mass; choice logit above 8 has 5.8x lift). It also ramps up sharply with trial index in the episode: zero before trial ~20, and half of the mass is in trials 90-99. So it reads like an a1-commitment signal that grows over the episode. Activation is higher when value is low (value under 5.2 gives 3.5x lift; none above 8.1). In the profile, the top windows tend to follow unrewarded trials or rare transitions (prev_common==0 has 2.2x lift), but adding prev_reward or prev_common terms hurt recall. It never fires on a2 choices or on D2 steps. Scored on dev: GO & model_act==1 gives mass recall 0.90 at precision 0.18. Adding ep_trial>=70 gives F1 0.58 and mass recall 0.85. Using value<7.1 instead of the ep_trial cut gives about the same F1 (0.57). F1 plateaus near 0.57, so precision is incomplete: many late-episode a1 GO steps stay silent, which points to some episode-level or hidden-state modulation that the predicate does not capture. The recorded predicate uses only observed variables and the policy output of the agent itself.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: last=a1 S2 r (+3.98), phase=D1 & last=a2 S2 r (+3.12), phase=GO & ep_dec=9 (+2.82), choice_bin=decile 8 (9 = most a1) (+2.73), phase=GO & value_bin=decile 0 (9 = highest) (+2.38), phase=GO & choice_bin=decile 9 (9 = most a1) (+2.37). Lower it: ep_dec=0 (-7.37), phase=D2 (-7.19), phase=GO & ep_dec=2 (-4.32), phase=D1 & last=a1 S1 r (-4.31).
